rules.title: Anti-Eviction Act good cause requirement
rules.requirement: A residential landlord may not evict a tenant or fail to renew a written or oral lease without good cause, and must be able to prove the grounds in court.
rules.coverage_text: Most residential rental properties, including single-family homes, mobile homes and land in a mobile home park, apartment buildings, complexes, and rooming and boarding homes.
rules.exemptions: May not apply to two- or three-unit owner-occupied premises with two or fewer rental units. Does not apply to hotel guests, motel guests, or guest houses rented to a transient guest or seasonal tenant, but hotel and motel guests are covered if they have no alternate residence and reside there on a continual basis. Does not apply to a unit held in trust on behalf of a developmentally disabled immediate family member who permanently occupies the unit.
rules.quoted_span: No residential landlord may evict or fail to renew a lease, whether it is a written or an oral lease without good cause. The landlord must be able to prove in court that he has grounds for an eviction.

rules.title: Written notice and Notice to Quit for good cause evictions
rules.requirement: Each cause for eviction, except nonpayment of rent, must be described in detail in a written notice to the tenant, and a Notice to Quit is required for all good cause evictions except for nonpayment of rent.
rules.coverage_text: Good cause evictions under the Anti-Eviction Act.
rules.quoted_span: Each cause, except for nonpayment of rent, must be described in detail by the landlord in a written notice to the tenant.

rules.title: Eviction for failure to pay rent
rules.requirement: A landlord may take legal action to evict for nonpayment of rent without prior notice, except that a 14-day notice must be given before filing if the tenant resides in federally subsidized housing. A tenant may not be evicted for nonpayment if the unpaid rent was used to continue utility services the landlord was responsible for and failed to pay.
rules.coverage_text: Tenants who fail to pay rent; notice requirement applies to tenants in federally subsidized housing.
rules.quoted_span: The landlord is not required to give the tenant notice before filing an eviction suit, except if the tenant resides in federally subsidized housing.

rules.title: Eviction for disorderly conduct
rules.requirement: If a tenant continues disorderly conduct after a written Notice to Cease, the landlord may file for eviction; a Notice to Quit must be served at least three days before filing.
rules.key_value: Notice to Quit at least three days prior to filing
rules.coverage_text: Tenants who continue disorderly conduct that destroys the peace and quiet of other tenants or the neighborhood after a Notice to Cease.
rules.quoted_span: A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least three days prior to filing a suit for eviction (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(b)).

rules.title: Eviction for damage or destruction to the property
rules.requirement: A tenant may be evicted for intentionally or through gross negligence causing or allowing destruction, damage, or injury to the property; a Notice to Quit must be served at least three days before filing.
rules.key_value: Notice to Quit at least three days prior to filing
rules.coverage_text: Tenants who intentionally or by gross negligence damage the property.
rules.quoted_span: The tenant may be evicted if they have intentionally or by reason of gross negligence caused or allowed destruction, damage, or injury to the property.

rules.title: Eviction for substantial violation of landlord's rules and regulations
rules.requirement: If a tenant continues to substantially violate reasonable rules in the lease or accepted in writing after a written Notice to Cease, the landlord may file for eviction; a Notice to Quit must be served at least one month before filing, on or before the start of a new month.
rules.key_value: Notice to Quit at least one month prior to filing
rules.coverage_text: Tenants who continue substantially violating reasonable lease rules and regulations after a Notice to Cease.
rules.quoted_span: A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least one month prior to filing the suit for eviction.
